I will mainly plant a winter wheat and summer maize rotation. In Quzhou County, this is the crop pattern I trust most because I know the land, I know the work rhythm, and the sales are steady enough. At the start of this season, my winter wheat is already in the field from last autumn, so I will focus first on topdressing, watering, and controlling disease and insects at the key stages. After harvesting wheat, I will sow summer maize quickly on the same land, because I want to keep the full year productive and reduce idle time.

I will use improved seed for wheat and hybrid seed for maize, because I care more about stable yield than saving seed. I will not push fertilizer blindly. I will give enough nitrogen for yield, with phosphorus and potassium to keep the crop standing and filling grain better. Water is important, but I will not over-irrigate. For wheat, I will irrigate around jointing and grain filling if moisture is short. For maize, I will water after sowing if needed and again around the big demand period before and after tasseling. I will manage pests by watching the field and spraying only when pressure is real, but I still expect to spray at least a couple of times on each crop in a normal year. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage because it fits my equipment and is less troublesome for me than deep ploughing every season.
